rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened day is initially identified as the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: مفعول ثان لأنذر وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers ask to be returned to worldly life and given a short reprieve so they can answer the call and follow the messengers they neglected.
rows.anchor: ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the day is their immediate destruction or death amid torment; then they ask that death or punishment be deferred briefly, as in 63:10.
rows.anchor: أو أريد باليوم : يوم هلاكهم بالعذاب العاجل ، أو يوم موتهم معذبين بشدة السكرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about their former oath can be heard as a spoken boast born of arrogance and ignorance, or as an implicit claim conveyed by building lasting homes and harboring distant hopes.
rows.anchor: أن يقولوا ذلك بطرا وأشرا ، ولما استولى عليهم من عادة الجهل والسفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their oath either asserted that they would remain in this world without death, or denied that they would be moved to another abode, thus denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزالون بالموت والفناء

words: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although سكن ordinarily takes في, Arabic also makes it transitive directly, as with تبوأ and أوطن; the underlying sense is dwelling or settling.
rows.anchor: يقال : سكن الدار وسكن فيها . ومنه قوله تعالى

words: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people settled comfortably in the former wrongdoers' homes, copying their injustice and corruption without recalling the earlier peoples' ordeals and endings to learn restraint.
rows.anchor: قروا فيها واطمأنوا طيبي النفوس ، سائرين سيرة من قبلهم في الظلم والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fate of earlier peoples had been made clear through reports and direct observation.
rows.anchor: بالإخبار والمشاهدة { كيف } أهلكناهم وانتقمنا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ونبين لكم, with the first-person plural verb.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ونبين لكم ) ، بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parables are descriptions of what earlier wrongdoers did and what was done to them, remarkable enough to serve as examples for every oppressor.
rows.anchor: أي صفات ما فعلوا وما فعل بهم ، وهي في الغرابة كالأمثال المضروبة لكل ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plotting is described as great, consuming all their effort.
rows.anchor: أي مكرهم العظيم الذي استفرغوا فيه جهدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction treats their plotting as the active genitive: it is recorded by God, who will repay it with a greater counterplot.
rows.anchor: أن يكون مضافا إلى الفاعل كالأول ، على معنى : ومكتوب عند الله مكرهم ، فهو مجازيهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the genitive is objective: God's plot against them is the punishment that reaches them unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: أو يكون مضافا إلى المفعول على معنى : { وعند الله مكرهم } الذي يمكرهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are an image for the enormity and intensity of the plot, as if it were capable of dislodging them.
rows.anchor: فضرب زوال الجبال منه مثلا لتفاقمه وشدته

words: وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also construes إن as negative and the lām as emphatic: their plotting cannot make mountains move; mountains can symbolize God's firm signs and laws, supported by Ibn Masʿūd's reading.
rows.anchor: وقد جعلت إن نافية واللام مؤكدة لها ، كقوله تعالى : { وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم }

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading وما كان مكرهم supports construing the clause as a denial that plotting could move the mountains.
rows.anchor: وتنصره قراءة ابن مسعود : ( وما كان مكرهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With lām of inception, another reading means that their plot was so forceful that mountains would be uprooted and shifted.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لتزول ) ، بلام الابتداء ، على : { وإن كان مكرهم } من الشدة بحيث تزول منه الجبال

rows.speaker: علي وعمر
rows.claim: ʿAlī and ʿUmar are reported to have read وإن كاد مكرهم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وعمر رضي الله عنهما : ( وإن كاد مكرهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not fail the promise to support His messengers, as promised in 40:51 and 58:21.
rows.anchor: يعني قوله : { إنا لننصر رسلنا } ( غافر : 51 ) ، { كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the promise before the messengers emphasizes that God never breaks a promise; naming His chosen messengers afterward makes failure toward them especially inconceivable.
rows.anchor: قدم الوعد ليعلم أنه لا يخلف الوعد أصلا ، كقوله : { إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts رسله in the genitive and وعده in the accusative; al-Zamakhsharī judges it weak, comparing it to the weak reading in 6:137.
rows.anchor: وهذه في الضعف كمن قرأ { قتل أولادهم * شركائهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عزيز means invincible and beyond being out-plotted; ذو انتقام describes His requital of enemies on behalf of His allies.
rows.anchor: { عزيز } غالب لا يماكر { ذو انتقام } لأوليائه من أعدائه

none: The segment contains only the quoted Qurʾānic passage, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ولها كتاب is an adjective of قرية; although the conjunction is not expected between adjective and noun, it emphasizes how closely the attribute adheres to its noun, like a circumstantial clause with عليه ثوب.
rows.anchor: جملة واقعة صفة لقرية ، والقياس أن لا يتوسط الواو بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known book is the village's appointed term, written and made known in the Preserved Tablet; 15:5 speaks of no community preceding its term.
rows.anchor: مكتوب معلوم ، وهو أجلها الذي كتب في اللوح وبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text first treats الأمة as feminine by form and then as masculine by meaning; عن is omitted after يستأخرون because it is understood.
rows.anchor: وأنث الأمة أولا ثم ذكرها آخرا حملا على اللفظ والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read تنزل with the sense تتنزل, also passive تنزل, and ننزل with nūn and الملائكة as its accusative object.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( تنزل ) ، بمعنى تتنزل ( وتنزل ) على البناء للمفعول من نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend only with wisdom and proper purpose; visibly appearing to testify for the Prophet would serve no wisdom because the audience would then believe under compulsion.
rows.anchor: إلا بالحق } إلا تنزلا ملتبسا بالحكمة والمصلحة ، ولا حكمة في أن تأتيكم عيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative explanations take الحق to mean revelation or punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحق الوحي أو العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا is both answer and consequence: it answers the demand and implies that, if angels came, the deniers would receive no reprieve and punishment would not be delayed.
rows.anchor: و { إذا } جواب وجزاء ، لأنه جواب لهم وجزاء لشرط مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening answers the mockery of 15:6 by asserting decisively that God Himself sent the Reminder through Gabriel to Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: رد لإنكارهم واستهزائهم في قولهم : { وقالوا يأيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guards the Quran from devils and from addition, omission, distortion, and alteration at every time; earlier scriptures were entrusted to rabbis and scholars, who altered them through envy and disagreement.
rows.anchor: محفوظا من الشياطين وهو حافظه في كل وقت من كل زيادة ونقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine preservation also demonstrates that the Quran is revealed: human speech would be exposed to additions and omissions like other speech.
rows.anchor: قد جعل ذلك دليلا على أنه منزل من عنده آية ؛ لأنه لو كان من قول البشر أو غير آية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun له to refer to the Messenger, as in God's promise to protect him in 5:67.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في { له } لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كقوله تعالى { والله يعصمك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means lest the earth tilt and shake with you; a مائد is someone made dizzy while traveling by sea.
rows.anchor: كراهة أن يميل بكم وتضطرب والمائد : الذي يدار به إذا ركب البحر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the newly created earth churned until mountains anchored it after the angels feared no one could live on it; the angels had not known what the mountains were made from.
rows.anchor: قيل : خلق الله الأرض فجعلت تمور ، فقالت الملائكة : ما هي بمقر أحد على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of rivers means God made rivers in the earth, since ألقى here carries the sense of جعل; 78:6 is a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: وجعل فيها أنهارا ، لأن { ألقى } فيه معنى : جعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are route markers, including mountains, watering places, and anything else travelers use to find their way.
rows.anchor: هي معالم الطرق وكل ما تستدل به السابلة من جبل ومنهل وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النجم is a generic singular referring to stars collectively.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنجم : الجنس ، كقولك : كثر الدرهم في أيدي الناس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the stars as the Pleiades, the two Furqad stars, the stars called Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي : هو الثريا ، والفرقدان ؛ وبنات نعش ، والجدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads وبالنجم with two dammas or with a damma and sukūn, as a plural of نجم; the sukūn lightens the form, with an alternative explanation that the wāw of النجوم was dropped for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( وبالنجم ) ، بضمتين ، وبضمة وسكون ، وهو جمع نجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting النجم and inserting هم mark Quraysh in particular: their special skill at navigating by stars made gratitude and reflection especially incumbent on them.
rows.anchor: قلت : كأنه أراد قريشا : كان لهم اهتداء بالنجوم في مسايرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some converts in Mecca were tempted by Satan to break their pledge because Quraysh prevailed over and persecuted Muslims and promised them rewards if they returned; God strengthened them.
rows.anchor: كان قوما ممن أسلم بمكة زين لهم الشيطان لجزعهم مما رأوا من غلبة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exchange God's covenant, the pledge to the Messenger, for the slight worldly inducement Quraysh offered to those who returned.
rows.anchor: ولا تستبدلوا { بعهد الله } وبيعة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { ثمنا قليلا } عرضا من الدنيا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God provides—victory and booty in this world and reward in the next—is better for them.
rows.anchor: { إنما عند الله } من إظهاركم وتغنيمكم ، ومن ثواب الآخرة { خير لكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people possess consists of transient worldly goods, whereas what God possesses from the stores of His mercy endures without end.
rows.anchor: من أعراض الدنيا { ينفد وما عند الله } من خزائن رحمته { باق } لا بنفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ولنجزين is read either with nūn or with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لنجزين ) بالنون والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient are those who endured the polytheists' abuse and the hardships of Islam.
rows.anchor: على أذى المشركين ومشاق الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular indefinite foot magnifies the danger: if one foot slips from the path of truth after standing firm, many feet slipping is all the more alarming.
rows.anchor: لاستعظام أن تزل قدم واحدة عن طريق الحق بعد أن ثبتت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what someone confides to another and what is more hidden: either what the person conceals inwardly or what they will later conceal in themselves.
rows.anchor: أي يعلم ما أسررته إلى غيرك وأخفى من ذلك ، وهو ما أخطرته ببالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view parses أخفى as a verb: God knows people's secrets and what He has kept hidden from them; al-Zamakhsharī rejects this as unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أن أخفى فعل يعنى أنه يعلم أسرار العباد وأخفى عنهم ما يعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the condition means loudly invoking God, the response teaches that He does not need loud speech: it either forbids loudness or teaches that it serves another purpose than making God hear.
rows.anchor: معناه وإن تجهر بذكر الله من دعاء أو غيره فأعلم أنه غني عن جهرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحسنى is the feminine form of الأحسن and describes the names because جمع غير العاقل is treated as feminine singular, as in مأرب أخرى and من آياتنا الكبرى.
rows.anchor: تأنيث الأحسن ، وصفت بها الأسماء لأن حكمها حكم المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names surpass others in beauty because they signify sanctification, glorification, majesty, and lordship, as well as the most perfect actions.
rows.anchor: والذي فضلت به أسماؤه في الحسن سائر الأسماء : دلالتها على معاني التقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Resurrection, though it may instead refer to prayer.
rows.anchor: أي : لا يصدنك عن تصديقها والضمير للقيامة ، ويجوز أن يكون للصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning tells Moses to affirm the Resurrection by naming the unbelievers' attempt to deter him, since their deterrence would lead to denial; alternatively, their attempt results from a believer's weakness, so mentioning it calls for firmness.
rows.anchor: أن صد الكافر عن التصديق بها سبب للتكذيب . فذكر السبب ليدل على المسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abundance of deniers should not shake Moses: their position follows desire and imitation rather than proof, so the passage urges evidence-based action and warns that blind imitation brings ruin.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا حث عظيم على العمل بالدليل ، وزجر بليغ عن التقليد ، وإنذار بأن الهلاك والردى مع التقليد وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūsā is parsed as a circumstantial accusative in the sense of pointing, as in 11:72; alternatively, تلك is a relative pronoun with بيمينك as its relative clause.
rows.anchor: في انتصاب الحال بمعنى الإشارة : ويجوز أن تكون { تلك } اسما موصولا صلته { بيمينك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks in order to show how He can transform dry wood into a writhing serpent, establish the great difference between the original and transformed things, and draw attention to His overwhelming power; the author compares it to a goldsmith displaying iron transformed into armor.
rows.anchor: إنما سأله ليريه عظم ما يخترعه عز وعلا في الخشبة اليابسة من قلبها حية نضناضة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads عصي, following Hudhayl's treatment of the final alif before yāʾ of the first-person suffix, with 12:19 cited as a parallel.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( عصي ) على لغة هذيل . ومثله { الرياح بشرى }

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads عصاي with a kasra on the yāʾ to meet the two sukūns, like 14:22; Ibn Abī Isḥāq is also reported to read the yāʾ without a vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( عصاي ) بكسر الياء لالتقاء الساكنين ، وهو مثل قراءة حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūsā leans on the staff when tired or stopped at the head of the flock, and when leaping.
rows.anchor: أعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع وعند الطفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هش الورق means striking or shaking leaves down for the sheep to eat; a saying attributed to Luqmān ibn ʿĀd uses هشة for a brittle twig, and نخب is a valley near Ṭāʾif.
rows.anchor: هش الورق : خبطه أي : أخبطه على رؤس غنمي تأكله

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī reads أهش; the author relates both forms to هش الخبز, bread breaking because it is brittle.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النخعي : أهش ، وكلاهما من هش الخبز يهش

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reads أهس with sīn, meaning that Mūsā drove the sheep with a call; الهس is the driving of sheep.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : أهس بالسين ، أي : أنحى عليها زاجرا لها . والهس : زجر الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūsā lists the staff's familiar uses in detail and summary as though sensing a great event to come, explaining it is ordinarily useful only like other sticks; alternatively, God elicits its many uses before revealing the far greater miracle.
rows.anchor: ذكر على التفصيل والإجمال المنافع المتعلقة بالعصا ، كأنه أحس بما يعقب هذا السؤال من أمر عظيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say God asked in order to put Mūsā at ease and reduce his apprehension.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إنما سأله ليبسط منه ويقلل هيبته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Mūsā gave a summary so God would ask about the uses and thereby honor him with further conversation.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إنما أجمل موسى ليسأله عن تلك المآرب فيزيد في إكرامه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say awe made Mūsā lose his speech and answer only in summary.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : انقطع لسانه بالهيبة فأجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report names the staff's wood as nabʿa.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : اسم العصا نبعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report lists extra staff functions: hooks and forks to gather branches or break them, carry gear, make shade, extend a short rope, and defend the flock from predators.
rows.anchor: كانت ذات شعبتين ومحجن ، فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report gives miraculous functions: drawing water by lengthening and becoming a bucket, lighting the night, fighting enemies, producing fruit or water, following Mūsā while carrying supplies, and protecting him from vermin.
rows.anchor: كان فيها من المعجزات أنه كان يستقي بها فتطول بطول البئر وتصير شعبتاها دلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السعي is swift walking with a light, quick movement.
rows.anchor: السعي : المشي بسرعة وخفة حركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different descriptions can mark stages: it first became a thin yellow snake (الجان), then swelled into a great serpent (الثعبان).
rows.anchor: أنها كانت وقت انقلابها حيه تنقلب حية صفراء دقيقة ، ثم تتورم ويتزايد جرمها حتى تصير ثعبانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it simultaneously had a serpent's large form and the jinn-like creature's speed; the author cites the description of it quivering like a jinn.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { فلما رءاها تهتز كأنها جان }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports add that the serpent had a crest like a horse's crest, or that the space between its jaws was forty cubits.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان لها عرف كعرف الفرس . وقيل : كان بين لحييها أربعون ذراعا

none: The segment contains only the verse text and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūsā warns them not to falsely call God's signs and miracles sorcery.
rows.anchor: أي لا تدعو آياته ومعجزاته سحرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is noted for فيسحتكم; سحت is the Hijazi form, while إسحات is used in Najd and by Banū Tamīm.
rows.anchor: قرىء { فيسحتكم } والسحت لغة أهل الحجاز . والإسحات : لغة أهل نجد وبني تميم

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's fragment إلا مسحتا أو مجلف is cited as evidence for the regional word form; the source notes a grammatical dispute over parsing its verse.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول الفرزدق :
. . . . . . إلا مسحتا أو مجلف ;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: والذي فطرنا can coordinate with ما جاءنا or function as an oath.
rows.anchor: { والذي فطرنا } عطف على ما جاءنا أو قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is recorded with قالوا لن نؤثرك على; the usual reading treats الحياة الدنيا as an adverbial expression and its syntax allows it to be construed like an object.
rows.anchor: قرىء { قالوا لن نؤثرك على } ووجهها أن الحياة في القراءة المشهورة منتصبة على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says there were seventy-two magicians, two Copts and the rest Israelites, and that Pharaoh had forced them to learn sorcery.
rows.anchor: وروي : أن السحرة يعني رؤسهم كانوا اثنين وسبعين : الاثنان من القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the magicians asked Pharaoh to show them Mūsā asleep; seeing his staff guard him, they concluded it was not a magician's trick because sorcery fails while a magician sleeps.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنهم قالوا لفرعون : أرنا موسى نائما ففعل ، فوجدوه تحرسه عصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تزكى means to purify oneself from the stains of sins.
rows.anchor: { تزكى } تطهر من أدناس الذنوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains تزكى as saying لا إله إلا الله.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : قال لا إله إلا الله

words: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three preceding verses are either a quotation of the magicians' speech or God's account rather than a quotation.
rows.anchor: قيل في هذه الآيات الثلاث : هي حكاية قولهم . وقيل : خبر من الله لا على وجه الحكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكذلك connects to كذلك نقص, saying that the Quran was revealed in the same manner as the preceding verses and, in fact, in its entirety on that pattern.
rows.anchor: عطف على ( كذلك نقص ) أي : ومثل ذلك الإنزال ، وكما أنزلنا عليك هؤلاء الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings are repeated throughout the Quran to lead people to leave sins or to perform good and obedience; ذكر can mean obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: مكررين فيه آيات الوعيد ليكونوا بحيث يراد منهم ترك المعاصي أو فعل الخير والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read نحدث or تحدث, with nūn or tāʾ; one reader also makes the thāʾ quiescent for ease, as in a cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( نحدث ) و ( تحدث ) بالنون والتاء ، أي : تحدث أنت . وسكن بعضهم الثاء للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exaltation magnifies God and the ordering of His servants through commands, prohibitions, promise, threat, reward, and punishment throughout His dominion.
rows.anchor: استعظام له ولما يصرف عليه عباده من أوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel recites revelation, the Prophet should wait until he hears and understands it, then retain it rather than racing Gabriel in recitation; alternatively, he should not convey a general passage before its clarification arrives.
rows.anchor: فتأن عليك ريثما يسمعك ويفهمك . ثم أقبل عليه بالتحفظ بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has حتى تقضى إليك وحيه.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( حتى تقضى إليك وحيه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for more knowledge expresses humility and gratitude for the instruction in proper learning, and asks for continuing increase because everything contains divine wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: { رب زدني علما } متضمن للتواضع لله تعالى والشكر له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that God commanded His Messenger to seek increase in nothing except knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما أمر الله رسوله بطلب الزيادة في شيء إلا في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In royal commands and instructions, تقدم إلى, أوعز إلى, عزم على, and عهد إلى are expressions for issuing an order or charge.
rows.anchor: يقال في أوامر الملوك ووصاياهم : تقدم الملك إلى فلان وأوعز إليه ، وعزم عليه

words: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's story follows the warning in 20:113: God had commanded him not to approach the tree and threatened him with the wrongdoers if he did, before the later people were warned.
rows.anchor: عطف الله سبحانه قصة آدم على قوله : { وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسي may mean forgetfulness, caused by failing to attend sincerely and secure the command in one's heart, or neglecting and abandoning the instruction to avoid the tree and its fruit.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد النسيان الذي هو نقيض الذكر ، وأنه لم يعن بالوصية العناية الصادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading vocalizes فَنُسِّي, making Satan the one who caused Adam to forget.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( فنسى ) أي : نساه الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عزم is firm resolve and persistence in refraining from eating, strong enough to leave Satan no hope of tempting him.
rows.anchor: العزم : التصميم والمضي على ترك الأكل ، وأن يتصلب في ذلك تصلبا يؤيس الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نجد may mean know, with له عزما as its two objects, or mean find as the opposite of lose, yielding the sense that Adam had no resolve.
rows.anchor: والوجود : يجوز أن يكون بمعنى العلم ، ومفعولاه { له عزما } وأن يكون نقيض العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وإذ is governed by an omitted verb, meaning remember the time of Satan's enmity, whispering, and beautification of eating from the tree.
rows.anchor: { وإذ } منصوب بمضمر ، أي : واذكر وقت ما جرى عليه من معاداة إبليس ووسوسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account shows that Adam was not steadfast in resolve: after prior advice and warning, he obeyed Satan, linking Adam's lapse with the larger lesson about firmness.
rows.anchor: حتى يتبين لك أنه لم يكن من أولي العزم والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Iblīs was a jinn, he was included in the command to the angels because he accompanied and worshipped with them; his lower rank made bowing all the more incumbent, as a lesser person should rise when the elite rise for a visitor.
rows.anchor: كان في صحبتهم ، وكان يعبد الله تعالى عبادتهم ، فلما أمروا بالسجود لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His exception from the angels works by collective usage that includes him under the angels' name, like saying everyone left except a woman among the men.
rows.anchor: عمل على حكم التغليب في إطلاق اسم الملائكة عليهم وعليه ، فأخرج الاستثناء على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبى begins a new sentence, as if answering why Iblīs did not bow; it needs no explicit object because the bowing is understood, and means he displayed refusal and hesitated.
rows.anchor: { أبى } جملة مستأنفة ، كأنه جواب قائل قال : لم لم يسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means that Satan must not become the cause of their expulsion from the Garden.
rows.anchor: فلا يكونن سببا لإخراجكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular hardship is assigned to Adam though both are expelled because the husband's hardship as household head includes his family, just as his happiness includes them; it also preserves the verse ending.
rows.anchor: لأن في ضمن شقاء الرجل وهو قيم أهله وأميرهم شقاءهم ، كما أن في ضمن سعادته سعادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hardship means toil in seeking sustenance, which falls primarily on the man and thus returns to Adam.
rows.anchor: أو أريد بالشقاء التعب في طلب القوت ، وذلك معصوب برأس الرجل وهو راجع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam was sent down with a red ox, plowed with it, and wiped sweat from his brow.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه أهبط إلى آدم ثور أحمر فكان يحرث عليه ويمسح العرق من جبينه
